title: A later accounting figure never rewrites what was actually approved or filed
summary: Accounting history is append-only. Tracking a stale or rejected filing, or a later/superseding figure, adds lifecycle observations and exact successor bindings; it does not rewrite the historical journals, attestations, snapshots or receipts. A superseded filing becomes immutable workflow evidence that cannot receive new lifecycle events.
evidence_note: CHANGELOG v0.8..v0.10 and REPORTING_LIFECYCLE_CONTRACT: immutable AccountingReportingFilingVersion distinguishes ORIGINAL/AMENDMENT/CORRECTION lineage, binds to exact snapshot/boundary and attestation identities, and carries SUPERSEDED/ACCEPTED/etc. lifecycle observations each bound to the exact prior fingerprint. v0.9 'proves later/backdated accounting can stale a historical report without destroying evidence of what was actually approved and filed.'
invariants: History is preserved append-only; a correction or later figure adds a bound lifecycle observation, it never edits the earlier record.
Supersession binds an exact successor filing fingerprint; resubmission binds an exact earlier submission event fingerprint.
Regulatory acknowledgement and decision events require exact external evidence identity.
An intentionally omitted detail stays omitted as evidence; it is never silently replaced by a guessed value (see qualifications on real Companies House filings).
